item.title: PM says BSP Life driving jobs and investment while company donates $150,000 to Wellness Coalition
item.description: As BSP Life celebrates it 150th Anniversary, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says investments by the organisation directly translate into employment opportunities, capacity building for local communities, and sustainable economic returns for resource owners and ensure that tangible benefits are meaningfully shared across communities, villages, and families throughout Fiji, creating a living legacy
item.content:encoded:
As BSP Life celebrates it 150th Anniversary, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says investments by the organisation directly translate into employment opportunities, capacity building for local communities, and sustainable economic returns for resource owners and ensure that tangible benefits are meaningfully shared across communities, villages, and families throughout Fiji, creating a living legacy of opportunity for future generations.

While speaking during the celebration at the Grand Pacific Hotel, Rabuka highlights that through the Yavu Collective and in partnership with Fiji Airways, they will open three new hotels over the next six months to complement its Sofitel asset on Denarau Island.

He also says a partnership with Dubai-based Kerzner International is planned to develop an ultra-luxury resort on Nacula Island in the Yasawas by 2029.

Rabuka says these developments will collectively elevate Fiji's position as a regional hub in the Pacific, further strengthening our tourism outlook on the international platform.

He says during peak periods, these major investments by BSP Life ensure that we have the world-class accommodation to meet growing demands and drive long-term economic growth.

Rabuka further says BSP Life's long-standing commitment to promoting financial security and long-term financial planning contribute directly to the national objectives of building a more inclusive, resilient, and financially empowered society.

The Prime Minister says by encouraging households to save, to invest, and plan for the future, the institution supports greater economic resilience at both the family and national levels.

He says as the nation's second-largest institutional investor after the Fiji National Provident Fund, the organisation plays a critical role in mobilising domestic savings and directing capital towards productive investments.

He says these investments support enterprise development, infrastructure, employment creation and broader economic activity, all of which are essential if Fiji is to achieve the sustained growth needed to realise its ambition of becoming a high-income economy by 2050.

Rabuka adds the government remains committed to working closely with responsible institutions such as BSP Life in advancing the priorities of the National Development Plan, expanding financial inclusion, strengthening economic resilience, promoting healthier communities, and increasing investment in the sectors that will drive sustainable growth.

BSP Life Group CEO Mark Robinson says they serve millions of customers through banking and insurance, united by a common purpose of championing prosperity for the South Pacific.

He says they recognize that the financial services landscape continues to evolve very rapidly, driven by changing customer expectations, emerging technologies and new market dynamics, both in Fiji, around the region and across the globe, customers expect greater convenience, more personalized services and sustainable value.

Robinson says BSP Life is investing in technology, strengthening its capabilities, optimising its group strengths and building for the future, while remaining true to the values that have earned the trust of generations of Fijians.

He says while technology continues to evolve, trust remains timeless.

Robinson says although the company is proud of its history, it is now entering the next chapter of its journey. He says the world ahead will be vastly different from the one it inherited, bringing new opportunities and challenges as a new generation of customers looks to institutions like BSP Life to help them achieve their aspirations.

Robinson also thanked BSP Life's customers across Fiji for their loyalty, saying many families have chosen the company for generations.

As part of their anniversary celebrations, BSP Life launched the Healthy Choices BSP Life Corporate Wellness Program and donated $150,000 to the Wellness Coalition to support its work in promoting healthy lifestyles across Fiji.

item.title: Corrections officers suspended with half pay over Lautoka Remand Centre incident
item.description: The four Fiji Corrections Service officers involved in an incident where an officer was seen in a social media video dragging an inmate into a dormitory before kicking and punching him several times, have been suspended with half pay. Fiji Corrections Public Relations Officer Jone Sigavou says the suspension was necessary to allow a thorough investigation to take place and ensure the process can p
item.content:encoded:
The four Fiji Corrections Service officers involved in an incident where an officer was seen in a social media video dragging an inmate into a dormitory before kicking and punching him several times, have been suspended with half pay.

Fiji Corrections Public Relations Officer Jone Sigavou says the suspension was necessary to allow a thorough investigation to take place and ensure the process can proceed without interference.

Sigavou says the officers were suspended yesterday following the incident at the Lautoka Remand Centre, which was captured on CCTV footage and later widely circulated on social media.

He says the duration of the suspension will depend on the outcome and completion of the investigations.

The Fiji Corrections Service says it maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of violence.

It says assaults by an officer against an inmate, or an inmate against an officer, are strictly prohibited.

item.title: Namalata calls for urgent road, bridge and water upgrades as flooding disrupts students' access to school
item.description: Namalata District Representative Ilaitia Savai is calling on the Government to fast-track road, bridge and water infrastructure projects, warning that damaged crossings continue to prevent about 20 students from attending school whenever river levels rise. Speaking to fijivillage News, Savai says improving roads and essential services remain a priority for the district in Tailevu.
item.content:encoded:
Namalata District Representative Ilaitia Savai is calling on the Government to fast-track road, bridge and water infrastructure projects, warning that damaged crossings continue to prevent about 20 students from attending school whenever river levels rise.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Savai says improving roads and essential services remain a priority for the district in Tailevu.

He is calling for Matacaucau Road to be upgraded, saying the Waterways Ministry has confirmed the engineering design for the project is currently being prepared.

Savai says this was raised during the Fijian Media Association Korovou Town Hall Forum and he hopes the design process will be completed soon so funding can be approved, and construction can begin without further delay.

He is also urging the Government to repair the seawall at nearby Sote Village, saying the area is home to a number of Ministry of Education staff and around 20 students who travel each day to attend Tailevu North College.

Savai says the district has repeatedly requested the reconstruction of two damaged crossings, as rising river levels often prevent students from getting to school.

He says a permanent bridge is urgently needed because schoolchildren, education officers and elderly residents rely on the crossing every day.

Savai also highlighted ongoing water supply issues, saying officials have confirmed plans to extend the water supply from Davetalevu.

However, he says while electricity has reached the area, communities as far as Burekasivi are still without a reliable water supply despite a growing population.

The District Representative acknowledged that work has begun on the Matacaucau Road following discussions held during the Fiji Media Korovou Town Hall Forum.

Savai, who has served as District Representative for the past eight months, says he has been pushing for development projects to benefit the district's 11 villages.

He also thanked the Government for electrifying most villages in Namalata, saying only Nailega and Yavusara are still waiting to be connected.

item.title: Plastic bags and wet wipes blamed for Suva wastewater overflow
item.description: Improperly disposed waste, including plastic bags, rags, wet wipes and clothing, caused a wastewater overflow along Cumming Street in Suva this morning. The Water Authority of Fiji says the overflow was caused by a pump failure at the Robertson Pump Station, which receives and transfers wastewater from the surrounding catchment area.
item.content:encoded:
Improperly disposed waste, including plastic bags, rags, wet wipes and clothing, caused a wastewater overflow along Cumming Street in Suva this morning.

The Water Authority of Fiji says the overflow was caused by a pump failure at the Robertson Pump Station, which receives and transfers wastewater from the surrounding catchment area.

WAF says the pump control float switches became entangled with large quantities of foreign materials that had entered the wastewater network, affecting the operation of the pumping system.

While the pump station is equipped with screening systems to ca pture such materials before they reach the pumps, WAF says the volume of foreign waste exceeded the screening capacity on this occasion, resulting in interference with the pump controls and a temporary failure.

WAF says their response teams attended the site immediately, rectified the issue, and completed disinfection and cleaning of the affected footpath and surrounding area.

The wastewater system has since returned to normal operation.

WAF is reminding people that the wastewater network is designed to carry only wastewater and human waste.

They say items such as wet wipes, diapers, sanitary products, rags, clothing, plastics, paper towels, cooking oils and other solid waste should not be flushed down toilets or disposed off into the sewer system.

WAF says improper disposal of these materials is a major cause of wastewater blockages, pump failures, manhole overflows and damage to critical infrastructure, creating public health and environmental risks.
